seo.title: Pricing — Cedar Mill Plumbing
seo.description: Flat-rate pricing on common plumbing service calls and free written estimates on projects $500+. Drain cleaning $189, water heater install from $1,650, leak detection $189, hydro jetting $499–$799.

header.heading:
Flat-rate on common calls.
Free written estimate on bigger projects.
header.lead: No diagnostic fees, no surprise add-ons, no commission upsell. Common service calls are flat-rate — same price whether the job takes ten minutes or an hour. Projects over $500 get a free written estimate before any work starts, and the number on that quote matches the number on the final invoice.

groups.label: Common Jobs
groups.blurb: Flat rates on the calls I run all week. Bigger projects (water heater swap, repipe, slab leak) get a free written estimate — see the next section.

tiers.name: Drain Cleaning
tiers.description: Branch drains — kitchen, bath, laundry — cleared with a cable. Same price whether it takes ten minutes or an hour. Mainline clearing through an accessible cleanout: $289 flat, includes a quick scope.

features.name: Camera scope after the line is open

tiers.name: Water Heater Install
tiers.description: Standard 50-gallon gas tank, code-correct, with new T&P valve, drip pan, expansion tank if required, and haul-off of the old unit. Electric 50-gal $1,890. Tankless conversion $4,800–$6,400 with a free written estimate.

features.name: Old unit hauled off, no separate fee
Same-day failure swap when truck has stock — +$150

tiers.name: Leak Detection
tiers.description: Full diagnostic visit: meter test, pressure isolation, acoustic listening, infrared on suspect walls, moisture mapping, and a written report with photos. Credited toward repair if you have me do the work.

oneOff.heading: Bigger projects — free written estimate.
oneOff.body: Anything over $500 in scope gets a free estimate visit. Whole-house repipe ($7,500–$14,500), tankless conversion ($4,800–$6,400), slab leak repair ($1,400–$3,800), cleanout install ($650–$1,200), hydro jetting ($499–$799 by line length). The estimate visit takes about 30 minutes. Written quote in your email by end of business that day, often faster. More on the FAQ →

faqs.question: Is there a diagnostic or trip fee on top of the repair?
faqs.answer: No. Flat-rate on common service calls means the rate covers everything — the trip, the diagnosis, and the repair. The only add-on is the after-hours fee ($125) on evenings, overnights, weekends, and holidays.

faqs.question: What if the job turns out to be bigger than expected?
faqs.answer: If something behind the wall changes the scope, I stop, walk you through what I found, and we agree on a revised number in writing before any additional work starts. No "already too far in" pressure tactics.

faqs.question: Do you take payment plans?
faqs.answer: For projects over $5,000 I accept a 30% deposit at scheduling with the balance on completion. For very large repipes I'm willing to break the balance into two payments. I don't run financing or third-party loan products — keeps things simple.

faqs.question: What does the warranty actually cover?
faqs.answer: Workmanship — if a joint I made fails or a fixture I installed leaks, I come back and fix it free. 1 year on standard work, 5 years on whole-house repipes. Parts are covered under the manufacturer's warranty (typically 6-12 years on water heaters, 25 years on PEX, lifetime on most quality fixtures); I file the claim if a covered part fails.

cta.heading: Have questions about whether the job needs an estimate or a flat-rate call?
cta.body: Easiest way is to call (503) 555-0149 or send a contact form with a few sentences about what's going on. I'll tell you straight whether it's a service call or worth an estimate visit.
